source_refs.note: Topic 6.4.3.1 (PDF 164, printed 161). The book calls crypto transactions private; the pseudonymity, volatility and legal-status notes are general knowledge, flagged.

blocks.text: Cryptocurrencies offer a decentralized way to exchange money: instead of being issued by banks, they use blockchain to record transactions in a way that cannot be changed, without middlemen. Bitcoin, Ethereum and others let people send money quickly and cheaply, even across borders, and can include people without access to banks.

The book says such transactions are private because they need no personal information. More precisely, a Bitcoin transaction is recorded publicly on the ledger under an address rather than a name, so it is pseudonymous rather than fully private. Cryptocurrency values can also swing sharply, and their legal status differs between countries.

blocks.prompt: Give one benefit and one risk of cryptocurrencies.
blocks.explanation: Benefit: fast, cheap transfers across borders without a bank. Risk: prices can change sharply, and lost keys or scams can mean money is lost for good.

items: Cryptocurrencies: decentralized money on blockchain (Bitcoin, Ethereum); transparent ledger, pseudonymous, volatile.
